How accurate are these 7 famous wildlife-inspired songs?

By Cottage Life Published: November 23, 2026
  • share
  • Share on Facebook
  • Share on Twitter
  • Share on Pinterest
  • Copy Link
Photo by Shutterstock/David Brickner

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:49
Instaread

Turns out, plenty of songwriters take inspiration from the wildlife world for their songs and lyrics. But how accurate are they? Let’s look at the evidence.

1) The Fox
Ylvis (2013)

Lyric: What does the fox say? Ring-ding-ding-ding-ding-eringeding!

Research shows that foxes say a lot: they bark, howl, scream, squeal, and gekker (chatter). They don’t say “ring-ding-ding.” Obviously.

2) Fly Like an Eagle
Steve Miller Band (1976)

Lyric: Fly like an eagle, to the sea.

Eagles do fly to the sea, and even swim. They use their wings to butterfly stroke through water when dragging heavy fish.

3) Fireflies
Owl City (2009)

Lyric: You would not believe your eyes, if ten million fireflies lit up the world.

Our gobs would be smacked if 10 million fireflies—roughly equal to the light from about 400 60-watt bulbs—lit up the entire earth.

4) Hungry Like the Wolf
Duran Duran (1982)

Lyric: I’m hungry like the wolf.

Wolves often eat sporadically, so, yup, they’re real hungry. A wolf can scarf the equivalent of about 80 McDonald’s Quarter Pounders in one meal.

5) Joy to the World
Three Dog Night (1970)

Lyric: Jeremiah was a bullfrog, was a good friend of mine.

Maybe someone did have a good friend who was a bullfrog. But frogs don’t drink wine. Or anything. They absorb water through their skin.

6) Muskrat Love
Captain & Tenille (1976)

Lyric: Muskrat Susie, Muskrat Sam, do the jitterbug out in muskrat land.

Muskrats perform courtship “dances” in the lake, but this in no way resembles the jitterbug. It’s closer to a water ballet duet. If you squint.

7) When Doves Cry
Prince (1984)

Lyric: This is what it sounds like when doves cry.

Doves don’t cry. But the mourning dove, named for its sad, cooing call, sounds unhappy 24/7. Fair enough, Prince.
